events.title: Fiscal Responsibility Act writes NEPA deadlines and page limits into law (BUILDER Act)
events.summary: Public Law 118-5, signed June 3, 2023, added NEPA Section 107 through its Title III 'Builder Act' (Sec. 321): lead-agency rules, a two-year deadline for environmental impact statements, page limits of 150 pages (300 for extraordinary complexity) for EISs and 75 for environmental assessments, and sponsor-prepared documents. Title III also covered energy storage permitting and the Mountain Valley Pipeline.
events.significance: Put NEPA deadlines and page limits in statute, the baseline that EO 14154 told CEQ and agencies to meet.

events.title: Senate ENR Committee advances the Manchin-Barrasso Energy Permitting Reform Act, 15-4
events.summary: The Senate Energy and Natural Resources Committee advanced S. 4753, the Energy Permitting Reform Act of 2024, by 15-4; Sens. Sanders, Wyden, Hirono and Hawley voted no. Chairman Joe Manchin and ranking member John Barrasso had released it on July 22 and introduced it July 23. It never received a floor vote and died with the 118th Congress.
events.significance: Paired limits on lawsuits with transmission and fossil-fuel permitting, the trade the 2026 Senate bill returns to.
actors: Joe Manchin (Senator, I-W.Va.; then ENR Chairman)
John Barrasso (Senator, R-Wyo.; then ENR ranking member)

events.title: D.C. Circuit panel says CEQ has no authority to issue binding NEPA regulations
events.summary: In Marin Audubon Society v. FAA, a divided D.C. Circuit panel vacated an air tour management plan for four Bay Area parks. In Part II, Senior Judge Randolph wrote that NEPA gives CEQ no authority to issue binding regulations; Chief Judge Srinivasan dissented from that part.
events.significance: Gave the incoming administration a judicial basis to argue that CEQ's 1978 NEPA regulations were not binding law.
actors: A. Raymond Randolph (Senior Circuit Judge, D.C. Circuit)

events.title: EO 14154 'Unleashing American Energy' directs CEQ to propose rescinding its NEPA rules
events.summary: On his first day, President Trump signed EO 14154, which revoked Carter-era EO 11991 (the basis for CEQ's binding NEPA regulations) and ordered the CEQ Chairman to issue NEPA guidance and propose rescinding CEQ's regulations within 30 days. It also told agencies to prioritize 'efficiency and certainty' in permitting and to streamline judicial review of NEPA.
events.significance: Started the executive-branch rollback of the NEPA regulatory framework that permitting legislation would later try to codify or replace.

sources.title: Unleashing American Energy (Executive Order 14154)

events.title: EO 14156 declares a national energy emergency and calls for emergency permitting
events.summary: EO 14156 declared a national emergency under the National Emergencies Act and told agencies to use emergency and other lawful authorities to expedite energy projects. It singled out the Army Corps' emergency permitting provisions, ESA emergency consultation regulations, and the ESA Committee.
events.significance: Agencies cited it for their compressed emergency reviews of energy and minerals projects.

sources.title: Declaring a National Energy Emergency (Executive Order 14156)

events.title: Presidential memo halts new wind leasing and orders review of wind permitting
events.summary: A presidential memorandum temporarily withdrew all Outer Continental Shelf areas from new or renewed wind leasing and ordered a review of existing wind leases. It also barred agencies from issuing new or renewed approvals, rights of way, permits, leases or loans for onshore and offshore wind projects pending a review of federal wind permitting practices.
events.significance: Opened the administration's wind-permitting freeze, which later became a major sticking point for Senate Democrats in permitting talks.

Council on Environmental Quality, the U.S. District Court for the District of North Dakota granted summary judgment to the plaintiff states and vacated CEQ's 2024 'Phase 2' NEPA rule. The court found that CEQ lacks statutory authority to promulgate binding rules implementing NEPA.
events.significance: A second court ruling that CEQ's NEPA rules lacked legal force; CEQ cited it when it removed its regulations three weeks later.
actors: U.S. District Court for the District of North Dakota

events.title: CEQ interim final rule removes its NEPA implementing regulations from the CFR
events.summary: CEQ published an interim final rule (90 FR 10610) removing its NEPA regulations, 40 CFR parts 1500-1508, effective April 11, 2025, with comments due March 27, 2025. The rule cited EO 14154, Marin Audubon and Iowa v. CEQ.
events.significance: Ended the government-wide NEPA regulations in place since 1978, leaving each agency to rely on its own procedures.
actors: Katherine R. Scarlett (Chairman, Council on Environmental Quality)

events.title: FERC Order No. 1920-B affirms the long-term transmission planning rule on rehearing
events.summary: FERC issued Order No. 1920-B, resolving rehearing of Order No. 1920-A (November 21, 2024), which had expanded states' role in the 20-year regional transmission planning rule first issued in May 2024. It clarified that transmission providers need not plan for unenrolled non-jurisdictional providers and kept the requirements tied to state-agreed cost allocation methods. Court challenges are consolidated in the Fourth Circuit.
events.significance: Kept the federal long-term transmission planning framework in place while the 2026 Senate bill proposes statutory changes to transmission planning and siting.

It also set expedited ESA Section 7 consultation and a seven-day Section 106 comment window under the National Historic Preservation Act.

events.title: Supreme Court, 8-0 in the judgment, narrows NEPA review in Seven County v. Eagle County
events.summary: The Supreme Court reversed the D.C. Circuit's vacatur of the Surface Transportation Board's environmental impact statement for the Uinta Basin Railway. Justice Kavanaugh's opinion says courts must give agencies substantial deference on NEPA reviews and that agencies need not analyze effects of separate upstream or downstream projects; Justice Gorsuch took no part.
events.significance: Made NEPA challenges harder to win. The Senate bill writes the same deference into the statute.
actors: Brett Kavanaugh (Associate Justice, U.S. Supreme Court)

events.title: Interior, DOE, USDA, DOT and Army Corps replace NEPA rules with streamlined procedures
events.summary: Following CEQ's rescission, the Departments of the Interior, Energy, Agriculture, Transportation (FHWA, FRA, FTA), Commerce and Defense, including the Army Corps, published interim final rules or new procedures on July 3, 2025; several moved most NEPA procedures into non-binding guidance. FERC's revised NEPA rules took effect August 18, 2025.
events.significance: Shifted NEPA implementation from government-wide binding rules to agency-specific procedures that, per Harvard's tracker, potentially exclude more projects from review and limit public comment.

events.title: One Big Beautiful Bill Act adds a paid, faster NEPA review option (Sec. 60026)

Sec. 60023 rescinded unobligated environmental review implementation funds, and the law also ended key wind and solar tax incentives.
events.significance: Added a statutory option to pay for a faster NEPA review, which CEQ's September 2025 guidance put into practice.

The bill clarifies what counts as a 'major federal action,' simplifies NEPA documents and sets judicial review limits including a 150-day deadline for filing claims.

events.title: CEQ issues new categorical exclusion guidance, replacing its 2010 guidance
events.summary: CEQ's April 9, 2026 memorandum on establishing, revising, adopting and applying categorical exclusions replaced the December 2010 guidance, which had rested on CEQ's now-removed 1978 regulations. It tells agencies to create categorical exclusions for categories of actions that normally lack significant effects, adopt other agencies' exclusions where appropriate, and consider exclusions before developing an EA or EIS.
events.significance: Pushed agencies toward wider use of categorical exclusions, the fastest NEPA track, under the 2023 statutory definition and adoption process.

events.title: Judge Casper enjoins five directives that stalled federal wind and solar permitting
events.summary: Chief Judge Denise Casper of the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts preliminarily enjoined five agency actions as likely violating the Administrative Procedure Act: Interior's July 15, 2025 secretary-review memo, a Fish and Wildlife Service database restriction, Secretarial Order 3438's capacity-density standard, an Army Corps memo and an Interior offshore order. Regional clean energy trade groups brought the case; the relief is limited to the plaintiffs and their members.

events.title: FERC issues show cause orders to all six RTOs on large-load interconnection
events.summary: In place of a single national rule, FERC voted unanimously on June 18, 2026 to issue Section 206 show cause orders to PJM, MISO, SPP, CAISO, ISO-NE and NYISO, preliminarily finding their tariffs may be unjust and unreasonable for lacking clear large-load and co-location provisions. Responses were due in 60 days, with generation-adequacy reports due in 30 days; DOE had asked for final action on its October 2025 proposal by April 30.
events.significance: FERC chose regional tariff changes over one national rule. The Senate bill would set a national cost rule by statute.

events.title: CEQ withdraws 18 NEPA guidance documents, including Forty Questions and 1997 EJ memo
events.summary: A Federal Register notice signed by CEQ Chairman Katherine Scarlett withdrew nine previously published guidance documents and nine agency memoranda, effective June 29, 2026, as obsolete after CEQ's rescission of its NEPA regulations, NEPA amendments, revoked executive orders and case law. They include the 1981 'Forty Most Asked Questions,' the 1997 environmental justice guidance and the June 2024 memo on the Phase 2 rule; CEQ will review whether any should be reissued.
events.significance: Cleared decades of CEQ guidance tied to the removed regulations, leaving the statute, agency procedures and CEQ's 2025-26 guidance as the NEPA framework.

events.title: House passes the Ratepayer Protection Act 417-3 on data-center electricity costs
events.summary: The House passed the Ratepayer Protection Act, introduced by Rep. Gabe Evans (R-Colo.), by 417-3 under a fast-track procedure requiring two-thirds. The bill encourages state utility regulators to set standards so large-load customers such as data centers pay for the new generation and infrastructure they require. events.title: Senate leaders release the 417-page Bipartisan American Affordability and Jobs Act
events.summary: Sens. Capito, Lee, Whitehouse and Heinrich released the 417-page bill at a press conference. It sets a 150-day limit for NEPA claims, bars agencies from revoking issued permits except in listed cases (Sec. 1401), and requires data centers to pay their transmission costs. Wind and solar 'regular order' terms remain under negotiation with the White House, with amendment work in parallel and a vote aimed for after the Senate returns in November.
events.significance: The first full bipartisan Senate text since the 2024 Manchin-Barrasso bill. The wind and solar question is unresolved.
